name: What size shower fits where a bathtub was removed?

mainEntity.name: What shower size usually fits in a former bathtub space in a standard Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: What shower size usually fits in a former bathtub space in a standard Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most standard tubs occupy a similar alcove footprint, so a shower can often fit within the existing opening. But the usable shower size is affected by wall finishes, waterproofing layers, base thickness, and whether the design includes a curb or curbless entry. Some homeowners are surprised that the final interior shower space is smaller than the old tub cavity once the walls are rebuilt. A contractor should measure the rough opening, not just the visible tub dimensions, before recommending shower pans, doors, or glass panels. In smaller bathrooms, thoughtful design can make the shower feel larger even if the footprint stays similar. Clear glass, light colors, and a simple layout often help. Homeowners should also think about how the shower opening aligns with adjacent fixtures so daily use stays comfortable. Measuring correctly at the start prevents ordering the wrong pan or enclosure.
acceptedAnswer.description: A typical tub alcove can often fit a shower around the same footprint as a standard tub, but the usable size depends on wall thickness, drain placement, and whether the design uses a curb, curbless entry, or glass enclosure. Exact dimensions should be measured on site.
